title: TCP: A Tensor Contraction Processor for AI Workloads Industrial Product
problem: Traditional AI accelerators rely on fixed-size matrix multiplications, limiting efficiency for diverse tensor operations. Exploiting data locality and parallelism in tensor contractions with varying shapes requires flexible hardware-compiler co-design.
motivation: Efficiently executing tensor contractions is critical for AI workload performance and power efficiency in production inference systems.
method: TCP has processing elements (basic compute units) that can combine into a single larger unit or operate independently, depending on the tensor shapes being processed. A circuit switch-based fetch network (a data-routing system similar to a telephone switch) enables data to be reused between different compute units, while input broadcast and buffers (temporary storage) maximize data reuse within individual units. The compiler automatically explores different configurations—adjusting tensor shapes, the order of operations, and hardware settings—to find the fastest combination for each workload.
key_novelty: The key innovation is a circuit switch-based fetch network (a flexible data-routing system, like a telephone switch) that enables compute units to reuse data from each other when processing tensor contractions (matrix-like operations on multi-dimensional arrays).
contributions: Tensor contraction processor architecture explicitly designed to exploit parallelism and data locality in AI workloads
Flexible processing elements reconfigurable between single-unit and multi-unit compute modes based on operation requirements
Circuit switch-based fetch network for dynamic inter-PE data routing and reuse
Compiler co-design that explores tensor shape and loop optimization jointly with hardware capabilities

metrics.speedup: 2.7× vs H100 and 4.1× vs L40s on performance-per-watt
metrics.other: 256/512/1024 TOPS (BF16/FP8/INT8 or INT4); 256 MB SRAM, 1.5 TB/s HBM3, 150W TDP

limitations: Limited discussion of scaling to multi-chip systems, generalization beyond LLM workloads, and real deployment considerations beyond LLaMA-2 inference.
primary_theme: Flexible tensor contraction accelerator for efficient LLM inference
